why: Here Benjamin means the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.

"People of Gibeon" (2:20) names a town, which is linked as a place, not the person Gibeon. Cherub and Immer (2:59) were places in Babylonia whose sites are unknown; Bible Atlas draws Cherub on Babylon and Immer at Nineveh in Assyria, which is a guess.
Here Israel means the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.

The text says "Beyond the River", the Persian province west of the Euphrates, not a river at Jerusalem; Bible Atlas puts its point on Jerusalem. Here Benjamin means the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.
